newsitem.title: UK: UK housing market recovery durable - CML.
newsitem.headline: UK housing market recovery durable - CML.

text.p: A strong pick-up in the number of owner-occupiers moving house since mid-1995 suggests the UK housing market recovery is durable and well-founded, the Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML) said on Monday.
"The likelihood is for a noticable increase in the number of people moving house over the next couple of years," said CML chief economist Bob Pannell in an article in "Housing Finance".

He said this plus a return to modest equity withdrawal by existing owner-occupiers implied an increase in net mortgage lending to existing owner-occupiers to 2.0 billion stg over the next few years compared with minus 2.0 billion stg in 1995.

"Increased activity and confidence on the part of moving owner-occupiers will play an important part in the UK's return to healthier levels of property turnover and further recovery in house prices over the next few years," Pannell said.
